A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TIDE study. All 23 pages of each version, including Appendices A–D, are readable and support comparison. Tables and figures can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original automatic evaluations of eight small language models, human empathy ratings from 116 retained participants, and demographic analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original automatic evaluations, 116-participant human study, and demographic results, including their appendix evidence.

M1.justification: The synthetic-dialogue generation approach, evaluated models, and LoRA fine-tuning procedure remain unchanged. Section 6.8 newly documents clinician involvement but does not establish a revised method. Knowledge distillation is proposed only as future work.

E1.justification: Both versions use TIDE's 10,000 two-turn dialogues across 500 personas and the same six human-evaluation scenarios. The U.S., first-language-English participant coverage and Appendix A survey prompts are unchanged.

E2.justification: The same eight SLMs are compared in zero-shot and fine-tuned conditions against Claude Sonnet 3.5 references. Appendix B retains the same model pairings; spelling and hyphenation changes do not introduce different comparators.

E3.justification: v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 1 specify identical 6,000/4,000 training/evaluation samples, three epochs, and training hyperparameters. Metrics, the six-prompt within-subject survey, response randomization, and participant-filtering rules remain unchanged. The pilot description becomes less specific without establishing a different procedure.

E4.justification: The same scenario-specific, demographic, regional, and response-example analyses are retained. Section 6.8 supplies clinical-validation documentation without new audit results. Adversarial and longitudinal testing remain unperformed rather than newly added evaluations.

E5.justification: v2 removes explicit Bonferroni-correction reporting for age, education, gender, and regional comparisons, including the adjusted thresholds stated in v1 Section 6.5. Reported p-values, effect sizes, mean/SD practices, sampling seed, and three-call LLM-judge procedure remain unchanged. This establishes reduced reporting, not necessarily changed computations.

E6.justification: Matched automatic scores, human win-table cells, demographic statistics, figure values, and Appendix A responses are unchanged. Section 5 in both versions reports 26 zero-shot versus 22 fine-tuned wins and 72/96 Claude wins. Relocated displays provide no additional result entries.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces formal theoretical results or proofs. Appendix C retains the same MAE definition and filtering conditions. Renaming the empathy ceiling and rewriting its explanation do not add mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain TIDE, evaluation of eight SLMs, uneven fine-tuning benefits, capacity limitations, and demographic variation in perceived empathy. The conclusion is unchanged apart from punctuation. The rewritten abstract and ceiling terminology reframe existing findings without establishing a different central empirical claim.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the applicability boundaries in Section 11: single-generator dependence, two-turn scope, nonclinical raters, and absent adversarial/crisis testing receive explicit treatment. It also adds an empathy–informativeness trade-off interpretation and discusses specialized models, while removing v1's explicit small-sample caution for regional findings.

D1.justification: v1 only promises dataset release; v2 adds a dataset location, CC BY-NC 4.0 license, and public-availability statement in Section 10, materially changing documented access. Section 6.8 adds clinician co-design, prompt-refinement, and auditing details. However, Section 4.2 still describes release as planned, and v2 removes the IRB-approval statements.

R1.justification: v2 removes the trauma-disclosure motivation and associated literature, including Frattaroli and Lucas, together with the Davis/Goleman grounding for the empathy framework. The six-part related-work survey and central positioning around trauma-specific SLM evaluation remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, motivation, related work, and substantial portions of the discussion are rewritten. Motivation is compressed, discussion headings change, and dedicated clinical-validation and data-availability sections are added. This is extensive narrative revision despite stable experiments.

P2.justification: The empirical displays are substantially redistributed: Figures 2–3 move from Appendix D into main-text pages 6–7, and v1 Table 4 becomes main-text Table 1. Remaining tables are renumbered and appendices reflow. The underlying figure images and result values are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves usability and interpretation through integrated empirical displays, documented dataset access, clearer clinician involvement, and explicit limits concerning short dialogues, nonclinical raters, and untested safety. These help readers assess and reuse the unchanged study. The gain is constrained by removed Bonferroni and IRB-approval reporting, reduced clinical grounding, and contradictory dataset-release statements; the revision adds no empirical validation resolving the study's substantive limitations.
